title: Traditional Turkish coffee is brewed slowly to build foam
body: The beans are ground very finely and heated slowly with cold water in a small pot. Sugar may go in before brewing. The coffee is served unfiltered, leaving the fine grounds in the cup.
takeaway: Reading shapes left by the grounds is part of the social tradition around the drink.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Turkish Coffee Culture and Tradition (2013)
visual: a small copper coffee pot beside a cup crowned with foam

title: A shake of the cup can decline more Arabic coffee
body: In the Arabic coffee traditions listed by UNESCO, hosts serve older people and guests before others. A guest may signal that they have had enough by shaking the small cup.
takeaway: The cup itself carries a social signal, so a guest can end the exchange without interrupting conversation.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Arabic Coffee, a Symbol of Generosity
visual: a guest gently tilting a small handleless coffee cup beside a brass pot

title: Maloya carries oral history on Reunion Island
body: Maloya combines song, music and dance on Reunion, an island in the Indian Ocean. It developed among enslaved people of African and Malagasy origin and was passed down through generations of performers.
takeaway: A performance can keep part of a community's history audible even when written accounts are scarce.
visual: a group of percussionists and dancers gathered on a Reunion Island terrace
